# S331 — Auto-land a passing run (per-project opt-in)

*Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-11. Size M. In the v1.1 relay the owner's standing rule was "land any slice whose gate returns `VERDICT: PASS` without asking". The orchestrator applied it by hand on every run: read `gate-N.md`, mark human checks "later", run `ork approve`, then push. This slice lets a project opt in to ork doing that step itself, within limits the owner sets. Push already exists (`ork projects set P --push on`, `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:311`).

**Findings:** Every v1.1 landing was a hand approve after VERDICT: PASS under the owner's standing rule. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-11** — [decision] Owner decision 2026-11-11 (adj 281, landing.auto-approve = default-for-all): when every gate passes (VERDICT: PASS, no open [owner] finding) and the checks are green, the run is approved. ork lands it and cleans up with no ork approve call, for every project. A per-project --auto-land off exists only as an opt-out. Human checks never block: at landing ork appends the run's human checks (including [AFTER LAND] ones) to human-checks-todo.md at the repo root, under '## ID (run RUN, DATE)' as '- [ ] TEXT' lines in the format the file already uses, and commits that file with the landing's tracking commit. Q1 = (a) as default-on for all; Q2 = (a) with checks going to the todo file, not marked later; Q3 is moot (adj 280: Check lines are implementer-runnable); Q4 = (a). The orchestrator lands passing runs by hand under this rule until this slice lands.

## Why

*Proposed.* Evidence:

- Owner, 2026-11-07: "land any passing slice without asking approval" (memory `landing-needs-no-approval`), and "Push after every landing". Every landing on 2026-11-08 to 11-11 followed the same hand steps: confirm `VERDICT: PASS` with `ork show RUN gate-N.md`, run `ork check RUN N later` for each human check, run any orchestrator-only Check lines (adj 263), then `ork approve RUN` and `git push origin main`.
- Adj 162 (`landing.in-ork`): ork lands after the owner approves. Auto-land changes who approves, so it needs a new adj record from the owner. It does not edit 162.

Open owner questions (the owner answers before the relay starts; key `landing.auto-approve`):
- Q1 whether to do this at all, and its default. (a) a per-project setting `ork projects set P --auto-land on|off`, off by default (recommended). (b) a per-run flag `ork run ... --auto-land`. (c) do not build it; the approve step stays by hand.
- Q2 human checks. (a) a run with human checks is auto-landed with each check marked "later", and the landed list shows them (recommended: it matches the hand practice in this relay). (b) any human check blocks auto-land.
- Q3 orchestrator-only Check lines (adj 263). (a) a run whose spec has any Check line not run by ork's checks is never auto-landed; it waits for `ork approve` (recommended). (b) auto-land anyway.
- Q4 which gate results count. (a) only `VERDICT: PASS` with no `[owner]` finding left open and the full check green (recommended). (b) as (a), plus a notice before landing.
